_meta.purpose: Expanded multi-doc evaluation set for Stage 2. Exists because Stage 1's multi-doc sample (n=4 gold, n=1 held-out) is too small to read a fine-tuning effect: at n=1 a single question flipping is a 100-point swing.
_meta.status: DRAFT — awaiting user review (Stage 2 Phase 2A Step 0 gate). No training data is generated until this is approved, because this set is the yardstick the whole fine-tune is measured against.
_meta.size_reasoning: 35 questions. Chosen so one question is worth ~2.9 points rather than 25 (n=4) or 100 (n=1), which makes a real effect distinguishable from noise, while staying small enough that every question could be hand-authored against verified source text rather than generated. 35 also gives ~8-9 per operation family, enough to break results out by operation type in 2C(i).
_meta.provenance: Every expected figure was read from the source PDF page text (PyMuPDF) and is quoted in verification_quote. No value was taken from the SQLite store, which is the artifact under test.
_meta.freshness: Deliberately built from facts NOT used by gold_set.json or holdout_set.json, even where the same document is reused. Document overlap is unavoidable (16-doc corpus) so freshness is enforced at the FACT level: e.g. FDIC contributes ROA 1.08% and NIM 3.17% here, never the $64.2bn net income used in gold P07/M03. See results/eval_expansion_notes.md for the full used-fact exclusion list.

operations.comparison: read a comparable figure from each of 2+ documents and contrast them
operations.aggregation: combine figures across documents into a total or joint statement
operations.contradiction: surface a conflict or period mismatch between documents
operations.lookup_then_combine: retrieve a fact from one document, use it to qualify a fact from another

_meta.scoring_note: answer_contains lists the figures that must appear. Both/all documents' figures are required, so answering from a single source scores as a miss — which is the exact M01/M02/M03 failure mode this set is built to measure.
_meta.design_note: REVISED after a self-check found the first draft had only 7 of 35 questions spanning two or more documents — the rest paired two facts from a single document, which does not test multi-doc reasoning at all. Rebuilt so 26 of 35 are genuinely cross-document. The remaining 9 are kept deliberately as SAME-DOCUMENT CONTROLS: if the fine-tune improves cross-document questions but not these, the gain is specific to multi-doc reasoning rather than to two-fact extraction generally. That distinction is what 2C(i) needs.
_meta.grading_note: Needles are matched as COMPLETE NUMBERS via src/eval_match.py, not by substring. Substring matching credited '1.36' for a '1.3' needle and matched a bare '5' inside '15.2'. That flaw was found by this set's dependency check and is fixed globally.

questions.question: Compare the FDIC net interest margin with the 12-month PCE inflation rate reported by the Federal Reserve.

questions.verification_quote: net interest margin (NIM) declined 10 basis points to 3.17 percent | PCE rose 2.4 percent over the 12 months ending in January
questions.replacement_note: Replaced during review. The original paired FDIC 3.17 with the Fed funds target range, whose only needle was a bare '5' - unusable, because the source writes the range with unicode fractions (5-1/4 to 5-1/2) leaving no clean numeric token, and '5' matches inside almost any number. Swapped for PCE 2.4, a distinctive token on the same page.
